title: DDIA 8 · THE TROUBLE WITH DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS
subtitle: On one machine, things either work or crash. Across machines you get partial failure: some parts work, some don't, and you often can't tell which.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.

blocks.text: The client only knows "no reply before the timeout". That is why every retried operation must be idempotent.
Last-write-wins compares timestamps, and the causally later write loses. No error is raised. NTP accuracy is only tens of ms at best.
Client 1 wakes up, checks nothing, and writes. Two writers think they own the lock.
A late writer with an old token is rejected. The protection is enforced by the resource, not trusted to the client.

items: "What if the payment provider times out?"
Outcome unknown. Retry with the same idempotency key, or reconcile with a status query. Never blindly charge again.
Fine for efficiency (avoid duplicate work). For correctness add fencing tokens, or use the DB's own conditional writes.
Wall clocks skew. Use a sequence from one leader, a Kafka partition offset, or logical clocks (Ch 9).
"How do you detect a dead node?"
Heartbeats + timeouts tuned to p99.9, and accept false positives. Leader election by majority, with epochs to fence the old leader.
